dimensions.label: Clarity and judgement
statements: I make clear which priorities can wait.
I make timely decisions even when I don’t have all the information.
I explain the trade-offs behind decisions that affect others.
dimensions.strength: You give people a clear sense of what matters and explain the choices behind a decision.
dimensions.growth: When several priorities compete, it can be hard to make the trade-offs visible to the people doing the work.
dimensions.action: For one live decision, write down what you’re deciding, which trade-off you accept, and what new information would make you revisit it.

dimensions.label: Influence across teams
statements: I speak to key stakeholders before asking for a decision in a formal meeting.
I adapt how I frame a proposal to the people affected by it.
I surface disagreement early enough to act on it.
dimensions.strength: You make time to understand other teams’ concerns and bring people into a decision early.
dimensions.growth: A proposal may reach the meeting before you have heard what it would mean for the people affected.
dimensions.action: Before your next cross-team decision, speak to one person whose support matters. Ask what would make the proposal difficult for their team.

dimensions.label: Strategic capacity
statements: I protect time to think beyond immediate delivery.
I drop or defer work that no longer serves a priority.
I tackle recurring problems rather than repeatedly resolving the latest instance.
dimensions.strength: You make room to look beyond this week’s delivery and address the causes of recurring problems.
dimensions.growth: Immediate demands can take the time you wanted to spend thinking beyond delivery.
dimensions.action: Block 30 minutes this week to identify one recurring issue you can address at the source.

dimensions.label: Delegation and ownership
statements: I make it clear who owns a decision.
I agree when someone should escalate without asking them to run every decision past me.
I resist taking work back when someone else can still deliver it.
dimensions.strength: You give people room to make decisions and agree when they need to involve you.
dimensions.growth: When ownership is unclear, decisions can keep finding their way back to you.
dimensions.action: Give someone ownership of one decision this week. Agree the outcome, their decision rights, and when to check in.

dimensions.label: Sustainable leadership
statements: I renegotiate commitments when new work exceeds capacity.
I notice when pressure starts to change how I lead.
I protect time away from work when things get busy.
dimensions.strength: You notice the effect of pressure and make deliberate choices about your commitments.
dimensions.growth: In a busy week, protecting time away or renegotiating commitments can become harder.
dimensions.action: Before accepting one new commitment, name what will move, who needs to agree, and what you’ll protect.
